questions.question: According to Roads & Roadless Areas in British Columbia, approximately how many kilometres of roads does B.C. have, and what road types are included?

expected_facts.text: Includes unpaved roads and trails allowing motorized vehicle use
The included trails allow motorized vehicle use

questions.reference_answer: B.C. has approximately 719,000 kilometres of roads, including all paved roads and unpaved roads and trails that allow motorized vehicle use.
questions.reviewer_note: Verified opening bullets on PDF page 1. Approximate total; do not treat trails without motorized access as included.

questions.question: In the British Columbia roads report, what percentage of roads are unpaved, and which surfaces are included in that category?
questions.reference_answer: Unpaved roads contribute 92 percent of total road length and include seasonal, loose and rough surfaced roads.
questions.reviewer_note: Verified page 2 prose, not inferred from graph ordering. Percentage describes road length.

questions.question: How does the B.C. report define roadless land, and what percentage and area of the province's landbase is roadless?

expected_facts.text: More than 500 metres from a road
accepted_phrases: more than 500 metres from a road

questions.reference_answer: Roadless land is more than 500 metres from a road. Sixty-six percent of B.C.'s landbase, or 62,600,000 hectares, is roadless.
questions.reviewer_note: Verified page 3 bullet. Use strictly more than 500 metres; page 1 also describes the share as two thirds.

questions.question: According to Ontario's 2022 road safety report, how many fatalities occurred in 2021 and 2022, and what percentage increase was reported?
questions.reference_answer: Ontario recorded 561 fatalities in 2021 and 623 in 2022, an increase of 11.1 per cent.
questions.reviewer_note: Verified page 10 table columns and adjacent prose. Manual review must check year-to-count mapping; phrase coverage cannot.

questions.question: What was Ontario's 2022 fatality rate per 10,000 licensed drivers?
questions.reference_answer: The 2022 fatality rate was 0.56 fatalities per 10,000 licensed drivers.
questions.reviewer_note: Verified 2022 table value and units. Do not confuse with the vehicle-distance-based international ranking on the same page.

questions.question: How many people were killed in Ontario collisions involving an inattentive driver in 2022, and what share of all fatalities involved inattentive driving?
questions.reference_answer: In 2022, 92 people were killed in collisions involving an inattentive driver; inattentive driving was a factor in 15 per cent of all fatalities on Ontario roads.
questions.reviewer_note: Verified paragraph on page 10. This is involvement as a factor, not proof of sole causation.

questions.question: What are the vision and slogan of Road Safety Strategy 2025 in Road Safety in Canada: Improving Your Safety?

expected_facts.text: The safest roads in the world
accepted_phrases: the safest roads in the world

questions.reference_answer: The vision is 'Towards Zero—The safest roads in the world' and the slogan is 'Rethink Road Safety'.

sources.section: The midpoint of Canada's Road Safety Strategy 2025

questions.reviewer_note: Verified page 4 prose. Strategy 2025 is discussed in this booklet; do not attribute it to unreadable charts in the separate 2025 filename.

questions.question: What minimum distance from the air bag and seating location for children under 13 does the Canadian safety booklet recommend?

expected_facts.text: At least 25 cm (10 in) away from the air bag

questions.reference_answer: Sit at least 25 cm (10 in) away from the air bag, and seat infants and children under 13 in the back seat.
questions.reviewer_note: Verified drivers/passengers and children recommendations on page 6. Reference summarizes booklet guidance, not independently verified current law.

questions.question: According to the Canadian safety booklet, by what percentages can correctly worn adult seat belts reduce the chances of death and serious injury in a collision?
questions.reference_answer: Correctly worn adult seat belts can reduce the chances of death in a collision by 47% and serious injury by 52%.
questions.reviewer_note: Verified page 7 adult figures (footnote 5), not the distinct child-restraint percentages. Manual review checks outcome-to-percentage mapping.

questions.question: What organization, database abbreviation and date are identified in the source line on the first page of the bundled Transport Canada 2025 PDF?
questions.reference_answer: The source line identifies Transport Canada - Road Safety, NCDB, dated August 12, 2025.
questions.reviewer_note: Verified literal extractable source line on page 1. No expansion of NCDB or numerical chart claims was inferred; the parser does not expose chart data.
